Two things beyond the shared floor SET are stated: SEQUENCING ("in order") and UNIVERSALITY ("every material professional transformation"). ASR-3's own SCOPE line makes materiality broad by default — "a result is material by default when it creates or changes professional content, supplies a downstream actor, proposes a Claim or Evidence, changes decomposition, contributes to a Decision/Baseline package, or supports a governed transition."

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `validateObligationConservation` (packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:62-84) unions exactly four sets — `allocated ∪ retained ∪ satisfied ∪ waived` (:65-68, :76-79) — over parent obligations whose `strength === 'MANDATORY'` (:74), and emits MISSING_OBLIGATION_ALLOCATION for any with none (:82). `buildObligationInput` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/decomposition.ts:146-172) is the ONLY production site that fills those four sets. TERM BY TERM, AS THAT BUILDER SUPPLIES THEM:

It maps the allocation record to its `obligationId` and DISCARDS `allocatedTo`. `ObligationAllocationSchema` is `{ obligationId, allocatedTo: string[] }` (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:306-309), so the field naming the children EXISTS on the wire and no predicate at this site reads it. DRIVEN: a decomposition whose only disposition of a MANDATORY obligation is `{obligationId: OBL, allocatedTo: []}` — allocated to NOBODY — was marked VALID; and one allocating to a PWU that is not among `childWorkUnitIds` was also marked VALID. The engine's OWN oracle takes the opposite reading over the same field: packages/rph-engine/src/graph-conformance.ts:105-107 counts an obligation unallocated when `!targets || targets.length === 0 || !targets.every((t) => children.has(t))`, with the comment 'Allocated to NOTHING, or to something that is not a child of this decomposition, is not allocation.' Two committed sites, one field, opposite answers — and the command gate uses the weaker one.

  TERM 2, 'retained by parent' — LIVE AND CHECKED. decomposition.ts:169 reads the contract's `retainedParentObligationIds`. CONTROL 1 (identical decomposition, obligation retained) was ACCEPTED and the contract reached VALID, which is what proves the refusal in PROBE 1 discriminates rather than fires for everything.

  TERM 3, 'already satisfied' — UNREACHABLE. decomposition.ts:170 sources it ONLY from `satisfiedObligationIds: objSatisfied`, and `objSatisfied` is filled at :162 by `else if (status === 'SATISFIED')` on the OBLIGATION object. `Obligation.status` can never hold that value: the only OBLIGATION command mints at PROPOSED (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/obligation-constraint.ts:34, births declared at :39) and no handler advances the machine. DRIVEN: after five dispatch attempts the obligation still read PROPOSED.

  TERM 4, 'explicitly waived/superseded by valid authority' — UNREACHABLE, AND 'valid authority' IS NEVER CONSULTED EVEN IF IT WERE. `authorizedWaiverObligationIds: objWaived` (:171) is filled at :163 by `else if (status === 'WAIVED')`; the 'superseded' half is the `continue` at :159 on `status === 'SUPERSEDED'`. No Decision, waiver object or authority reference is loaded on this path (contrast `buildConstraintInput`'s `authorityBasis` at :250-256, which DOES resolve a DECISION — the obligation half has no counterpart).

ROUTE 1 — OBLIGATION SATISFACTION ITSELF. `Obligation.status` declares SATISFIED and ALLOCATED (packages/rph-contracts/src/enums.ts:530-538) and packages/rph-domain/src/transitions.data.ts:951-970 declares the arrows ACTIVE->ALLOCATED and ACTIVE|ALLOCATED->SATISFIED, the first carrying THIS LIMB as its guard string. NO COMMAND EMITS ANY OF THEM. The single OBLIGATION command mints at PROPOSED and there is no `advanceStatus` for the machine anywhere. So no child — indeed nothing at all — can move an obligation to SATISFIED, with or without allocation.

ROUTE 2 — THE CHILD-SIDE COVERAGE ASSERTION, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT COULD HAVE LAUNDERED IT. `CoverageClaimSchema { claimId, parentObligationIds, childWorkUnitIds, coverageType, rationale }` (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:195-201) is EXACTLY the shape 'these children cover these parent obligations', it rides on ProposeDecomposition (messages.ts:465), and it is STORED AND ECHOED by the handler (decomposition.ts:67 and :103). It is read by NO predicate. DRIVEN (PROBE 7): a decomposition asserting `coverageType: 'COMPLETE'` over the MANDATORY parent obligation by the child, with no allocation and no retention, was REFUSED — the obligation still counted as MISSING_OBLIGATION_ALLOCATION. THE CONTROL IS BYTE-ADJACENT AND ISOLATES THE ONE FACT: the same contract, same coverage claim, PLUS `obligationAllocations: [{obligationId: OBL, allocatedTo: [CHILD]}]`, was ACCEPTED to VALID. Explicit allocation is the only thing that moved.

ROUTE 3 — THE INTENT MAPPING. `IntentMappingSchema.servesParentIntentOrObligationId` (objects.ts:292) lets a child declare it serves a named parent OBLIGATION. DRIVEN (PROBE 6): the child declared it serves the obligation ('the child discharges the parent obligation'), the decomposition was accepted, the mapping was stored verbatim — and the obligation's status was PROPOSED before and PROPOSED after. The field has ONE occurrence in the entire non-test, non-dist source tree: its own schema declaration.

WHY THIS ARM AND NOT ENFORCED_DRIVEN — THE EM-1 DISCIPLINE, APPLIED AGAINST MY OWN BEST PROBE. PROBE 7 is a real refusal and it is tempting to claim it. I do not. In its own terms the refusing predicate is 'this obligation id is in none of allocated/retained/satisfied/waived' — a set-membership test that never reads `coverageClaims`, never reads `childWorkUnitIds`, never reads `allocatedTo`, and would refuse identically with no coverage claim present at all (that is PROBE 1, limb 2's arrangement). The coverage claim was INERT. So the engine does not REFUSE a child's claim to satisfy a parent obligation; it never CREDITS one — enforcement by non-reading, which is this arm and not the other. Stated plainly, as the repository states it for RPH-TRC-004: the rule holds because there is nothing that could violate it, which is a guarantee and is not the same as a guard.

THE LIMB IS TOTALLY ADMITTED, DRIVEN AND OBSERVED — NOT PARTIALLY, AND NOT AT A DEAD SITE.

WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: a child PWU introducing work beyond parent intent WITHOUT AUTHORIZATION reaching a decomposition that is neither rejected nor routed to a human decision.

WHAT I BUILT, over-determined so no reading of 'beyond parent intent' escapes it: a parent PWU whose intent is 'a field service scheduling module for our 40 technicians' and whose boundaries name 'national-enterprise workforce optimization' in outOfScope; a child PWU whose intentId is a SECOND, foreign Intent captured with exactly that expression, whose parentWorkUnitId names the parent, and whose own boundaries.inScope is verbatim the parent's outOfScope entry; and a DecompositionContract whose intentMappings CONFESSES the enlargement on the wire — servesParentIntentOrObligationId points at the foreign intent, rationale reads 'the child enlarges scope beyond the parent intent'. This is DOC-008 §788-801's own worked example ('a child PWU introduces national-enterprise workforce optimization without authorization'). NO AUTHORIZATION EXISTS: the whole store held 7 events and not one DECISION object, so the limb's 'without authorization' qualifier is satisfied by construction of the fixture rather than assumed.

WHAT THE ENGINE DID: ProposePwu ACCEPTED. ProposeDecomposition ACCEPTED. ValidateDecomposition{disposition:'VALID'} ACCEPTED, producedEventIds ['e20'], contract status VALID. Zero events in the store match /DIVERG|FINDING|SCOPE_EXPANSION|HUMAN_DECISION/. Canon's disjunction offers two acceptable outcomes and the engine delivered neither.

WHY THIS IS NOT A DEAD-PREDICATE ROW even though a dead predicate exists. packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:555-559 does implement the rule, with severity REQUIRES_DECISION mirroring canon's 'routed to human decision' — and it cannot fire, for TWO independent reasons: its host composition validateDecomposition is imported by no non-test file, AND its input field intentDivergentChildIds appears on no wire schema (ProposeDecompositionPayloadSchema, messages.ts:456-468, is a z.strictObject of eleven fields and does not include it). But UNENFORCED_DEAD_PREDICATE would understate what I measured: I did not merely show the check cannot fire, I sent the arrangement and watched the engine accept it. That is the same correction the enforcement register itself made on 2026-08-03 when it re-guarded RPH-DEC-004 from a DEAD_PREDICATE census to an OBSERVED_ADMISSION, having demonstrated that wiring the composition into handlers/decomposition.ts left all 2078 tests green.

WHY NOT ENFORCED_MULTI_SITE: no set of sites covers it. Census (3) shows no production code anywhere compares a child's intent to its parent's; the parent/child relation is read only for EXISTENCE (pwu.ts:275, decomposition.ts:46) and for the recomposition parent lookup (pwu.ts:522-523).

So the question is whether the plane EXISTS, and the answer is: a shape for it exists in the kernel, the plane itself does not, and BOTH facts are already recorded in committed, gated files. Hence PARTIAL_DIVERGENT_FILED rather than UNENFORCED_NO_SHAPE (there IS a shape) and rather than DIVERGENT_UNFILED (it IS filed).

THE HALF THAT EXISTS. packages/rph-domain/src/presentation.ts declares the plane in so many words: `PresentationBearing extends SemanticSnapshot { readonly revision: number; readonly layout?: unknown }` (:13-16), and `applyPresentationChange` (:38-43) returns `{ ...obj, revision: obj.revision + 1, layout: newLayout }` under the docblock 'swap the layout and bump the DISPLAY revision, leaving semanticVersion and assuranceState untouched'. So there is no persisted layout to version, and therefore no revision plane for it.

THE FINDING THE FILINGS DO NOT YET CARRY — and it is the sharpest thing in this row. The kernel's 'own plane' is named `revision`, which is the SAME NAME as the store's optimistic-concurrency aggregate revision (packages/rph-persistence/src/schema.ts:74, sqlite-storage-adapter.ts:26/166/181, EnvelopeSchema `revision: RevisionSchema` at envelopes.ts:54) — the counter that EVERY semantic write bumps and that PER-4's `expectedRevision` check reads. So `applyPresentationChange` bumping `revision` would move the SEMANTIC concurrency plane, which is the precise arrangement 'layout has its OWN revision plane' exists to prevent. It is harmless only because the function is dead and never reaches the store. That collision is filed nowhere.

(ii) The note is not a passing remark about document drift — its second clause is a claim about the REPOSITORY ('the plane this repository does not have'), and it quotes the canon clause verbatim so the filing cannot drift from what it files against. Adding a new uncalled kernel function reddens this file' — so the day anyone wires `applyPresentationChange`, that file turns red and the disposition must be re-argued. evidence:
CANON OFFERS A DISJUNCTION — 'invalidates OR forces review' — AND THE ENGINE DELIVERS THE SECOND DISJUNCT, AT ONE PLANE ONLY.

FORCED REVIEW, DRIVEN. I caused a genuine semantic change to a subject the only way production can: two real authoring commands (DefinePwuType + EditPwuType) moved the PWA from semanticVersion 2 to 4 AFTER all three de minimis floor assessments had completed SATISFIED against v2. PublishPwa was then REJECTED, and the refusal names the remedy in the limb's own terms: 'Record a satisfied floor ... for the current version before publishing.' The prior assessments are NOT invalidated — each still loads assessmentState SATISFIED — but they are stripped of authority over the changed subject and a fresh review at the current version is demanded. That is 'forces review of prior assessments', and canon's disjunction admits it. CONTROL: the identical drive with the post-floor edit omitted publishes cleanly (ACCEPTED, publicationStatus PUBLISHED), so the refusal is discriminating on the semantic change alone.

WHAT IS NOT ENFORCED. Nothing recomputes, flags or re-opens a prior ASSESSMENT OBJECT when its subject moves. The assessment aggregate carries no staleness field and no handler revisits one; the whole effect is a downgrade computed at read time inside floorGateBlock, at two protected transitions and nowhere else. On the PWU satisfaction path the antecedent is not even detectable: I censused every semantic-version write and only INTENT, DECOMPOSITION_CONTRACT and PROFESSIONAL_WORK_ARCHITECTURE can move theirs — a PWU's is 1 at creation and every PWU commit path passes `newSemanticVersion: loaded.semanticVersion`. So a PWU's content can be revised (ReviseDecomposition, ApplyTacticalChange, ReshapePwu) while its version stands still, and no prior assessment of it is ever reviewed.

THE ONE READ-MODEL ANALOGUE, AND WHY IT IS NOT THIS. rph-projections/src/assurance-view.ts `foldInvalidation` annotates assessments SUBJECT_INVALIDATED and its docblock even cites 'invariant 16 (a subject change invalidates/reviews prior assessments)'. Do not expose blind retry; inspect/reconcile or discard this in-process candidate.", and the machine performs it — CONFLICTED and COMMIT_FAILED both have exactly one outgoing edge, DISCARD. In the domain proper, a retry is a first-class governed COMMAND, not a loop: `retryExecutionStep` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/execution.ts:1505) is dispatched by an actor, gated by `stepAuthorityRefusal` (plan-ACTIVE per RPH-EXE-002, the `retryDecision` cap per RPH-EXE-008, and a refusal when the last failure class does not permit RETRY), loads CURRENT state through `loadOrReject`, and emits its own event — so it is neither silent nor operating on stale assumptions. It is worth being precise about "silently", because an event IS appended and the append-only log does record THAT the write happened: what is silent is the TRANSFER — nothing records that caller A's decision rested on a superseded read, and neither actor is informed. evidence: WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: an aggregate's event history containing a gap, or being other than strictly ordered. THE ARRANGEMENT IS INEXPRESSIBLE FROM THE WIRE, and I established that from both ends rather than by reading one function. FROM ABOVE: no command carries an event revision. `DomainCommandSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/envelopes.ts:100-110) has no such field, and the census of every production write of `aggregateRevision:` shows all of them derived in-handler — `newRevision` (which is `loaded.revision + 1`, the cited site), literal `0` on the create path, or `i + 1` for the `alsoEvents` follow-on loop at kit.ts:660. Not one takes a value from `command.payload` or from the envelope. FROM BELOW: `ctx.store.commit` has exactly ONE production caller repository-wide — `commitState` at packages/rph-application/src/handlers/kit.ts:529 — so there is no second write path that could choose a revision. DRIVEN: three dispatches against one INTENT produced aggregateRevision sequence [0,1,2] with event types IntentCaptured, IntentDiscoveryStarted, IntentProvisioned, and the object's own revision landed on 2. Ordering on read is likewise structural: `readAggregateEvents` (packages/rph-persistence/src/sqlite-storage-adapter.ts:254) is `ORDER BY aggregate_revision ASC`, over a column with `UNIQUE (aggregate_type, aggregate_id, aggregate_revision)` and a supporting index (packages/rph-persistence/src/schema.ts:103,106). WHAT THE STORE ITSELF PERMITS, MEASURED DIRECTLY RATHER THAN INHERITED, because the register's RPH-PER-005 makes a specific claim and [[verify the recorded remedy]] says a recorded remedy is a hypothesis until driven. I called `store.commit` directly with an event whose aggregateRevision was 99 on an aggregate at revision 0: it returned {ok:true} and left the stream [0,99]. CONTROL over the same population, so the probe is known to be capable of both answers: the identical direct commit with a CONTIGUOUS aggregateRevision of 1 also returned {ok:true} and left [0,1] — so the {ok:true} on the gap is the store genuinely not checking, not the probe being malformed. The DUPLICATE half diverges differently: a second event at aggregateRevision 0 was REFUSED, but by the UNIQUE constraint throwing a raw SqliteError out of `commit` rather than returning a CommitResult — `CommitResult` has exactly one failure reason (`REVISION_CONFLICT`) and no way to return this one. SO THE HONEST SHAPE IS: canon's property holds for every reachable arrangement, and it holds because of how the revision is DERIVED, not because anything checks contiguity — nothing anywhere does. That is precisely what ENFORCED_BY_CONSTRUCTION means, and the store-level facts are already filed (see owed).

HALF ONE — THE ENGINE SEAM SATISFIES THE LIMB, AND I DROVE IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT. I built a second Engine over the same store (process restart, database survives) and confirmed that professional decisions are re-derived from durable rows, not carried in process memory: (a) the RPH-EXE-008 retry cap refused the third attempt AFTER the restart, and it can only have counted by folding ExecutionStepStarted events out of the store (`attemptsMadeFrom(ctx.store.readAllEvents(), ...)`); (b) an idempotency key first used before the restart returned status DUPLICATE with no new event from a brand-new Engine, so the receipt is a `command_receipts` row and not a Map; (c) the §36.2 failure-class refusal reads `ctx.store.readAggregateEvents(...)`. Handlers receive `ctx.store` and nothing process-scoped. Census of module-level mutable containers in the decision path (packages/rph-application/src, rph-domain/src, rph-engine/src, rph-persistence/src, tests excluded) returns 14 bindings and every one is a frozen constant vocabulary — ReadonlySet/Set of enum members (FLOOR_POLICY_ID_SET, ESCALATABLE_SEVERITIES, LIVE_CONSTRAINT_STATUSES, AI_STEP_TYPES, BLOCKING_SEVERITIES, PROMOTABLE_DISPOSITIONS, ...) — never written after initialisation. No cache, no session map, no memo.

HALF TWO — AND IT IS WHY THIS ROW IS NOT A CERTIFICATION. THE LIMB HAS TWO CLAUSES AND THE ENGINE SATISFIES THE SECOND ONLY BECAUSE THE FIRST IS VACUOUS.

CLAUSE A — 'Risk proportionality governs assurance'. The ONLY production predicate anywhere that reads a risk LEVEL is the RISK_AT_LEAST op of the DOC-007 §18 ApplicabilityExpression grammar (packages/rph-assurance/src/applicability.ts:71-78). It resolves `$.riskProfile` off the subject it is handed and compares the level index. It has exactly TWO production call sites, and BOTH hand it a subject projection from which riskProfile has been dropped:

So `resolvePath(subject,'$.riskProfile')` is `undefined` on every dispatch, applicability.ts:73 returns false, and the comparison at :77 (`actualIdx >= requiredIdx`) is UNREACHABLE. The predicate is stuck FALSE regardless of what any command puts on the wire.

I created three ACTIVE above-floor policies differing only in their applicability expression, and two PWUs at the extremes of the ratified ladder — HI = {consequence CRITICAL, uncertainty CRITICAL, irreversibility CRITICAL, securitySensitivity HIGH, regulatoryExposure HIGH}, LO = {LOW, LOW, LOW, NONE, NONE}, both read back off the store to confirm they persisted. THE LIMB HAS TWO HALVES AND I SCORED THEM SEPARATELY.

HALF ONE — 'an EXPLICIT, TESTED judgment in its handler'. It is explicit in a handful of handlers and silent in the rest, and the silence is load-bearing because the default is 'not semantic'. `advanceStatus`'s option is `readonly bumpSemanticVersion?: boolean;` (kit.ts:730) — OPTIONAL, so a handler that says nothing is read as declaring its command non-semantic. Of the 105 registered command types, exactly 5 carry an explicit positive declaration: ReviseIntent (`bumpSemanticVersion: true`, intent.ts:329), ReviseDecomposition (decomposition.ts:495) and DefinePwuType / EditPwuType / RemovePwuType (via `withPwaVersionBump` at pwa-authoring.ts:483, 734, 818). ZERO command types carry an explicit NEGATIVE declaration — `bumpSemanticVersion: false` occurs nowhere in the repository. Of 42 direct `advanceStatus` call sites exactly 1 mentions the flag at all, against 46 that declare a `precondition` — so on the very same construct, the precondition judgment is universally declared and the semantic judgment is declared once. Twelve commits pass `newSemanticVersion: loaded.semanticVersion` explicitly, which is a token but a mechanical carry-forward rather than a stated judgment. And 'TESTED' is thinner still: ten assertion sites in the whole repository assert a semanticVersion VALUE, of which the three that pin 'it did not move' (command-reissue-guard.test.ts:257, decomposition-revise-conservation.test.ts:175, dwp03-precondition-coverage.test.ts:364) all pin it after a REFUSED command, and the one that pins a presentation change leaving semantics alone (properties.test.ts:313) runs on `applyPresentationChange`, which has ZERO production callers. So NO committed test asserts that an ACCEPTED, non-semantic command leaves semanticVersion unchanged.

HALF TWO — 'objective, boundary, obligation, and decomposition changes are semantic'. DECOMPOSITION is honoured (ReviseDecomposition bumps the contract, decomposition.ts:495). OBLIGATION is honoured at the allocation level (`HONOURED_REVISION_FIELDS` = obligationAllocations, constraintPropagations on the same bumping path). evidence:
THE LIMB NAMES THREE CLASSES THAT MUST NOT BE SEMANTIC. ONE IS HONOURED; TWO ARE VIOLATED, AND I DROVE BOTH VIOLATIONS.

RETRIES — HONOURED. Driven: a plan taken to ACTIVE, its step STARTED then FAILED, then `RetryExecutionStep` -> ACCEPTED, plan revision 4 -> 5, semanticVersion 1 -> 1. No execution handler reaches a bump: `execution.ts:1020` passes `newSemanticVersion: loaded.semanticVersion` and EXECUTION_PLAN is not one of the three types that can ever raise a version.

FORMATTING — VIOLATED, DRIVEN. `EditPwuType { pwuTypeId, name: 'Root (renamed)' }` — a payload carrying ONE field, a human-readable display name, and nothing else — was ACCEPTED and raised the owning PWA's semanticVersion from 4 to 5. Canon's own OBJ-3 NON-EXAMPLE says display names 'are encouraged — they simply are not identity'; presentation.ts:1-4 in this repository states the rule this limb carries: 'A presentation/layout change … MUST NOT alter an object's semantic version or its assurance state.' The renamed PWU_TYPE itself stayed at semanticVersion 1; it is the PWA — the object a floor review BINDS — whose version moved for a cosmetic edit.

LAYOUT MOVES / NODE ORDERING — VIOLATED, DRIVEN. `EditPwuType { pwuTypeId, permittedChildTypeIds: [C2, C1] }` — the SAME SET of child type ids in reversed ORDER — was ACCEPTED and raised the PWA from 5 to 6. `permittedChildTypeIds` is 'the authoritative flat edge list (render/projections consume it)' (pwa-authoring.ts:442) and nothing reads its ORDER as meaning: every production consumer takes `.length` or set membership (pwa-authoring.ts:283, :764, :860). presentation.ts names this exact class verbatim — 'canvas position, NODE ORDERING, a display-only revision bump'.

THE MECHANISM, AND WHY IT CANNOT DISCRIMINATE. `withPwaVersionBump` wraps definePwuType/editPwuType/removePwuType UNCONDITIONALLY; the cited comment declares the judgment for the whole command ('Redefining a PWU Type materially edits the PWA's graph') and `bumpPwaSemanticVersion` (pwa-authoring.ts:125-199) never inspects WHICH field changed. Its docblock says the bump exists so that floor-gate's `versionOk` (`rec?.version === opts.subjectVersion`) can catch a PWU Type 'smuggled into' a reviewed graph. The consequence of not discriminating is that the same guard now invalidates a satisfied floor review because someone fixed a typo in a node's label.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE INVERSE OF THE ONE THE MECHANISM WAS BUILT FOR, AND THE VERSION CANNOT TELL THE TWO APART. CONTROL E in my run: `EditPwuType { completionRule: 'ALL_CHILDREN_COMPLETE' }` — a genuinely material change — raised the PWA 6 -> 7, the same single increment the rename produced. A reader of the PWA's version history sees four identical +1 steps and cannot distinguish 'a type was renamed' from 'the completion rule changed'; the events do not help either, because every bump emits the same `PwaEdited` with payload `{pwaId}` and nothing else (transcript below).

THE ABSENCE HALF IS REAL AND I AM NOT USING IT TO SOFTEN THIS. There is no persisted layout field anywhere — `layout`/`canvas`/`position` occur zero times across packages/rph-contracts/src, and the strict payload schemas actively refuse one (`EditPwa.safeParse` with a `layout` key -> unrecognized_keys). So a DEDICATED layout command cannot violate this limb. The violation arrives through a GENERAL edit command carrying a purely presentational patch, which is a route no dedicated-command census can see.

I DROVE CANON'S OWN NON-EXAMPLES, WORD FOR WORD, AND THE ENGINE ACCEPTED BOTH.
  C1 `statement: 'looks reasonable'`, severity MATERIAL, no evidence, no criterion -> ACCEPTED. Persisted object: criterionId ABSENT, evidenceIds [], implication === statement.
  C2 `statement: 'could be improved'`, severity CRITICAL -> ACCEPTED. Same shape.
  C3 `statement: ''` — an observation naming NO deficiency at all, at severity BLOCKING -> ACCEPTED. `statement: z.string()` has no `.min(1)`.
An authoritative ASSURANCE_OBSERVATION now exists in canonical state, disposition OPEN, whose entire content is the string 'looks reasonable'.

THE COUNT, PART BY PART, EACH ANSWER DRIVEN RATHER THAN READ OFF THE SCHEMA.
  1 SUBJECT — PRESENT but never NAMED by the observation: `subjectObjectIds` is INHERITED from the assessment (assurance.ts:2356) and there is no command field for it.
  2 POLICY — PRESENT but likewise inherited, and with a FALLBACK that can make it false: `policyId: assessment.assurancePolicyId ?? p.assessmentId` (assurance.ts:2355) writes the ASSESSMENT'S OWN ID into the policy slot when the assessment cites no policy.
  3 CRITERION — INEXPRESSIBLE. `RecordAssuranceObservationPayloadSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:352-359) has six keys and `criterionId` is not among them; the handler never writes it. DRIVEN: C4 supplying `criterionId: 'crit-1'` -> VALIDATION_FAILED (strictObject). The field exists on the OBJECT schema as optional and is written by nothing.
  4 EVIDENCE OR EXPLICIT PROFESSIONAL JUDGMENT — NEITHER IS REQUIRED AND ONE HAS NO FIELD. `evidenceIds` is optional and defaults to [] (driven: C1/C2/C3 all persisted with `evidenceIds: []`). There is NO professional-judgment field anywhere; DRIVEN: C6 supplying `professionalJudgment` -> VALIDATION_FAILED. So canon's disjunction has one optional-and-empty arm and one absent arm.
  5 SEVERITY — GENUINELY ENFORCED. `severity: AssuranceSeveritySchema`, required. DRIVEN CONTROL C7: `severity: 'MEH'` -> VALIDATION_FAILED.
  6 PRECISE DEFICIENCY — the field exists (`statement`, required) and the word 'precise' has no enforcement: '' and 'looks reasonable' both pass.
  7 IMPLICATION — INEXPRESSIBLE, AND WORSE THAN ABSENT: THE ENGINE FABRICATES IT. There is no command field (DRIVEN: C5 supplying `implication` -> VALIDATION_FAILED), and the cited line writes `implication: p.statement` — the object reports a consequence that is a verbatim copy of the deficiency. Every observation in the store therefore satisfies a required §21 field with a value nobody supplied, and the read-back cannot tell a real implication from the copy.
SO: 3 of 7 parts carry real values (subject, policy — both inherited — and severity); 1 of 7 is present but unconstrained (deficiency); 3 of 7 are INEXPRESSIBLE (criterion, evidence-or-judgment as a disjunction, implication). And the limb's operative clause — 'vague findings are non-conformant' — has ZERO enforcement: census for any vagueness/quality check across the whole engine returned 0 with an observed non-zero control.

THE CONTROLS PROVE THE SITE IS ALIVE, so the admission is not a dead boundary. The cheap evidence first: rail 1 is a FIELD on two object types (PWU_TYPE.requiredAssurancePolicyIds, PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT.assurancePolicyIds); rail 2 is its own object type VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_ENTRY (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:787) with its own declared machine ValidatorRegistryEntry.status (packages/rph-domain/src/transitions.data.ts:2329) and five named commands that touch nothing else (RegisterValidator / MarkValidatorDegraded / RestoreValidator / DisableValidator / EnableValidator); rail 3 is ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT with the AssuranceAssessment.state machine. No command writes two of them; no field is shared.

THE EXPENSIVE HALF — I WENT LOOKING FOR A CONFLATION AND FOUND THE OPPOSITE PROBLEM (the rails are so separate they never meet). Three driven arrangements:
(i) lane-ASR-18a.mjs: FOUR VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_ENTRY objects registered ACTIVE, collectively supporting every policy in the store, plus all four policies seeded/ACTIVE — and the assessment rail did not move an inch: PublishPwa still REJECTED with 'floor.schema-invariant=MISSING, floor.identity-provenance=MISSING, floor.reasoning-review=MISSING'. Registering capability writes nothing on rail 3.
(ii) lane-ASR-18b.mjs: VID_OK is registered ACTIVE with supportedPolicies=['pol_unrelated']. It then completed an assessment whose assurancePolicyId is 'pol_declared' — ACCEPTED. So rail 2's capability DECLARATION places no constraint whatever on rail 3.
(iii) The two fields that could join rail 2 to rail 1 — supportedPolicies and requiredCapabilities — are WRITE-ONLY (census below). Nothing derives an assignment from a registration or vice versa.

THE ONE POINT WHERE RAILS 2 AND 3 TOUCH is Gate D (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:2141-2145), which loads the registry entry named on the incoming ValidatorResult and refuses it when status === 'DISABLED'. That is a bounded read of ONE field (status), documented at assurance.ts:2117-2123 as deliberately NOT joining the evaluator/validator namespaces ('Joining them would be inferring a binding from proximity'). A bounded read is not a conflation; it is the rails meeting at a contracted seam.

The cited site is where the separation is HELD IN CODE rather than merely described: validator-registry.ts is the whole of rail 2's write surface and it imports nothing from the assurance handlers.

SITE 1 — `floorGateBlock` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/floor-gate.ts:305-322), reached from pwaFloorGate on PublishPwa (pwa-authoring.ts:962-976) and from the execution-plane completeExecutionStep gate. It reads NO policy attachment and NO registry entry.

I DROVE THE FORBIDDEN ARRANGEMENT AT ITS MAXIMUM (lane-ASR-18a.mjs): rail 1 fully in place (all three floor policies seeded and ACTIVE, plus an extra ACTIVE policy attached to the root PWU Type), rail 2 fully in place (FOUR VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_ENTRY objects registered, every one ACTIVE, collectively supporting every policy in the store), rail 3 absent (zero assessments). The refusal therefore keys on the ASSESSMENT and discriminates: 'a policy exists' and 'a validator is configured' were both true in the refused case.

SITE 2 — `rejectUnbackedDisposition` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwu.ts:1356-1379), on ChangePwuState. Setting assuranceState to any of {SATISFIED, CONDITIONALLY_SATISFIED, REJECTED, ESCALATED} requires citing an ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT whose assessmentState equals the asserted value and whose subjectObjectIds include the PWU. DRIVEN (lane-ASR-18b.mjs): a PWU carrying an attached policy and sitting in assuranceState ASSESSING, asked for SATISFIED with supportingObjectIds:[] -> REJECTED / RPH_EVIDENCE_MISSING. An attachment alone can never turn the assurance axis green.

Site 1 covers only the three FLOOR policies, only at protected transitions, and only when the subject is AI-produced OR has already been assessed (floor-gate.ts:307, `if (!opts.aiProduced && latest.size === 0) return null`). Together they close limb 4 for every path I could put on the wire; separately neither would.

THIS LIMB'S SUBJECT IS THE FIXING MECHANISM, NOT THE ARRANGEMENT. The repository HAS one — `TRACE_DIRECTIONALITY` (packages/rph-domain/src/traceability.ts:27-92), a 17-relation table that fixes exactly what this limb says, correctly: `SUPPORTS: { source: ['EVIDENCE','ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT'], target: ['CLAIM'] }` (:51) and `VERIFIES: { source: ['ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT'], target: ['CLAIM','PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT','BASELINE'] }` (:53-56). Its own vocab record states the provenance: packages/rph-domain/vocab/m6-traceability.json:163 — "AUTHORITATIVE on source: §25.1 'VERIFIES must originate from an Assessment.'" — and :372 names SUPPORTS and VERIFIES among the four relations §25.1 HARD-CONSTRAINS. THE PREDICATE THAT READS THE TABLE CANNOT FAIL IN PRODUCTION, AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN ASSERTING IT.

PROOF 1 — THE ARGUMENTS ARE CONSTANTS AT THE ONLY REACHABLE CALL SITE. `validateLinkDirectionality` has exactly one non-test caller: `TraceGraph.addLink` at traceability.ts:151, and `addLink` has exactly one non-test caller: `supportsGraph` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:585-606), reached from `invalidateEvidence` at assurance.ts:642. Read the call: `graph.addNode({ id: evidenceId, objectType: EVIDENCE })` (:596), `graph.addNode({ id: claimId, objectType: CLAIM })` (:597), `graph.addLink({ …, relation: 'SUPPORTS', … })` (:598-603). All three arguments the predicate receives — relation, source type, target type — are the literals 'SUPPORTS', 'EVIDENCE', 'CLAIM' on every execution. `validateLinkDirectionality('SUPPORTS','EVIDENCE','CLAIM')` is `{ok:true}` unconditionally. THE ONE CHECK THAT FIXES SUPPORT AND VERIFICATION BY TYPE IS ASKED THE SAME QUESTION EVERY TIME, AND IT IS THE ANSWER 'YES'.

PROOF 2 — I DROVE THE VIOLATING ARRANGEMENT THROUGH THAT EXACT PREDICATE AND IT PASSED. `ProposeEvidence` with `supportsClaimIds:[<a PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT>]` → ACCEPTED; `InvalidateEvidence` on it → ACCEPTED, and it emitted `EvidenceInvalidated{affectedClaimIds:["pwu_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69GR201"]}`. Producing that value REQUIRED `supportsGraph` to run `addNode({id: <the PWU>, objectType: CLAIM})` — fabricating the target's type — and then `addLink` to put a SUPPORTS edge through `validateLinkDirectionality`, which returned ok. THE SAME PREDICATE, ASKED THE TRUE TYPES IN THE SAME SESSION, REFUSES: `validateLinkDirectionality('SUPPORTS','EVIDENCE','PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT')` -> `{"ok":false,"reason":"SUPPORTS target must be one of CLAIM, got PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT"}`. The rule is correct, alive, and never asked the question that would make it fire.

PROOF 3 — A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEADNESS MECHANISM. `addLink` validates only `if (s && t)` (traceability.ts:150): when either endpoint is not a registered node, the check is SKIPPED ENTIRELY and the link is pushed. Driven: `new TraceGraph().addLink({id:'l1',relation:'SUPPORTS',from:'a',to:'b'})` with no `addNode` → no throw, and `outgoing('a')` returns the link. The handler's own docblock at assurance.ts:582-583 is aware of this — "omitting them would silently skip the check that makes the graph trustworthy" — and its remedy is to supply the types itself, as constants, which is proof 1.

WHAT IS NOT DEAD, NAMED SO THIS ROW IS NOT READ AS 'NO TYPE RULE EXISTS ANYWHERE'. Two handler-local filters do fix a type: assurance.ts:704 `if (e.aggregateType === EVIDENCE)` fixes the ORIGIN of the claim-status support path, and pwu.ts:1362 fixes the ORIGIN of a PWU's assurance verdict to ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT (driven, scored at limb:REL-2:2). But they are per-handler and demonstrably non-uniform — 'what may verify' is type-checked at pwu.ts:1362 while 'what may support' has NO target check at any surface — which is exactly the state this limb's word FIXED forbids. A rule that holds where a particular handler happens to have written it is not a rule fixed by type; it is 25 separate rules, and this limb's own artifact for stating it once is the table that nothing asks.

(a) A CORRECTION TO packages/rph-domain/src/enforcement-register.ts:2760-2765 (the RPH-TRC-005 row), which is wrong on the mechanism and wrong on the attribution. The register's own reason for not filing is dissolved by the canon rule this limb comes from. Following the retire-by-striking convention, the sentence should be struck in place with the correction beneath it, not deleted.

(b) A REG-F entry naming JPWB-DOC-003 §5 REL-2 limb 3: the repository's single artifact that fixes support and verification by type — `TRACE_DIRECTIONALITY` (traceability.ts:27-92) with `validateLinkDirectionality` (:100-120) — is correct, unit-tested (traceability.test.ts:20-43, which asserts exactly the SUPPORTS refusals this limb needs) and UNFAILABLE in production, for two independent reasons that must BOTH be stated or a partial fix will look like a whole one: (i) its sole reachable call site supplies all three arguments as constants ('SUPPORTS', 'EVIDENCE', 'CLAIM' at assurance.ts:596-600), so 1 of the table's 17 rows is ever selected and it is selected with a literal that always passes; (ii) `addLink` skips validation entirely when either endpoint is unregistered (`if (s && t)`, traceability.ts:150), driven.

THE REMEDY SHAPE SHOULD BE IN THE FILING, because the obvious one does not work. 'Make `supportsGraph` read the real objectType from the store' is necessary and NOT sufficient: `supportsGraph` runs only inside `InvalidateEvidence`, so a mis-typed endpoint would be caught at invalidation time — long after the object was minted, and only for evidence that is ever invalidated. Until then, a change to the SUPPORTS or VERIFIES rows of that table changes nothing observable in the engine, which is the property this row records.

THE LIMB HAS FIVE CONJUNCTS AND THE ENGINE HOLDS THREE. I drove all five.

HELD (1) — 'returns ... a *recommendation*'. The only wire word for the verdict is `dispositionRecommendation`, bound to `AssuranceDispositionRecommendationSchema` = {SATISFIED, CONDITIONALLY_SATISFIED, REJECTED, INCONCLUSIVE, ESCALATED} (packages/rph-contracts/src/enums.ts:96). `parseCompletion` refuses anything outside it at assurance.ts:1805 and the schema refuses it earlier: I dispatched CompleteAssuranceAssessment with dispositionRecommendation 'WAIVED' and got VALIDATION_FAILED / RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED before a handler ran. So a validator cannot name the one disposition canon reserves to Governance — the recommend/decide split is closed at the enum.

HELD (2) — 'a REPLACEABLE implementation'. Gate D at assurance.ts:2145 refuses a result whose validatorId is DISABLED in the registry, and its message names the clause: '§34.1's response to a failed validator is an ALTERNATE implementation'. Driven with TWO controls in separate worlds: ACTIVE -> ACCEPTED, DEGRADED -> ACCEPTED (impaired is not withdrawn), DISABLED -> REJECTED.

HELD (3) — 'of a VERSIONED Assurance Policy'. `ValidatorResultSchema` is a z.strictObject requiring policyId AND policyVersion (objects.ts:349-366); neither is optional and a strictObject rejects extras. NOT CLAIMED HERE: that the version is COMPARED to the assessment's — that is ASR-12's subject and is already recorded UNENFORCED_DISCLOSED as RPH-ASR-010.

ADMITTED (4) — 'evaluates IDENTIFIED Claims against IDENTIFIED Evidence'. `ClaimAssessmentResultSchema = z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (objects.ts:74) — a claim result need not name a claim. And nothing resolves `evidenceConsideredIds`. DRIVEN: a completion carrying claimResults:[{utter:'garbage'}] and evidenceConsideredIds:['evd_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69GABS'] (an id that resolves to no object in the store) was ACCEPTED, assessment SATISFIED, and the absent id was written verbatim into the AssuranceAssessmentCompleted event.

ADMITTED (5) — 'returns SCHEMA-CONFORMANT findings'. `ProposedAssuranceObservationSchema = z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (objects.ts:94). DRIVEN: observations:[{not:'a finding at all'}] was ACCEPTED — and the findings were then DROPPED ENTIRELY: zero AssuranceObservationRecorded events resulted, because the completion handler reads `next.observationIds` off the aggregate and never mints an observation from the validator's proposal. A finding shape that nothing validates and nothing consumes.

evidence:
A FOUR-WAY NEGATIVE. Scored one clause at a time; three hold, one is admitted on the wire.

(a) 'NEVER MUTATE PROFESSIONAL STATE' — HOLDS, by construction and driven. Exactly ONE payload in the entire message surface carries a validator's output (messages.ts:223, CompleteAssuranceAssessment), its targetAggregateType is ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT, and `commitState` (kit.ts:401) writes exactly one `args.aggregateId` per dispatch — the engine has no multi-aggregate write. DRIVEN: before/after a completion, the PWU is revision 0 -> 0, semanticVersion 1 -> 1, assuranceState UNASSESSED -> UNASSESSED, workLifecycleState PROPOSED -> PROPOSED; the CLAIM stays OPEN; the EVIDENCE stays ADMISSIBLE; and the event log shows the dispatch wrote the assessment aggregate and nothing else. Corroborated the other way: `command-bus.ts` resolves one handler per dispatch and the only event fan-out is a read-only `EventSubscriber = (event) => void`, so no accepted validator result can mint a second command (the register states this at enforcement-register.ts:1069-1072 for RPH-ASR-001).

(b) 'NEVER RETURN ONLY PROSE' — HOLDS. There is no free-text verdict channel: the verdict is `dispositionRecommendation`, enum-bound; `limitations` and `residualUncertainty` are string arrays that no gate and no projection treats as a verdict. Driven negatively: a non-enum recommendation ('WAIVED') dies at the schema.

(c) 'NEVER RETURN ONLY PASS-FAIL' — ⚠ ADMITTED, AND THIS IS THE ROW'S FINDING. DRIVEN: a completion in which EVERY content field is empty — claimResults [], observations [], evidenceConsideredIds [], evidenceRejected [], residualUncertainty [], limitations [], recommendedControlActions [] — was ACCEPTED and the assessment settled SATISFIED. What remains on such a result is identity (validatorId/version, policyId/version, assessmentId, subject + version) plus ONE enum value. That is the bare verdict canon forbids; the only thing standing between it and literal pass/fail is that the enum has five members rather than two, and nothing in the engine requires a single one of the content fields to be non-empty. The rule IS honoured one layer down, in the FLOOR kernel's own `ValidatorResult` (packages/rph-assurance/src/floor.ts:89-115), whose `criteria: readonly FloorCriterion[]` is a typed CriterionResult array and whose docblock states the canon clause verbatim — but that typed criterion detail is explicitly dropped at the wire boundary, which is the filed divergence.

(d) 'NEVER RETURN UNSCOPED CONFIDENCE' — VACUOUSLY HELD, and I will not dress that up as enforcement. `ValidatorResultSchema` has no confidence field at all, so a validator cannot return confidence of any kind. `AssuranceAssessment.confidence` exists (objects.ts:569) and no production line writes it; the only payload that could carry one, AssuranceAssessmentSatisfiedPayloadSchema (messages.ts:908), belongs to an event this engine never emits. See census.

(e) 'VALIDATOR OUTPUT NEVER GRANTS PERMISSIONS' — HOLDS, driven at full strength. `ControlActionSchema` DOES include ACCEPT and PROMOTE_BASELINE, so a validator can literally recommend the acts limb 3 reserves. Two independent barriers, both driven: Gate B (assurance.ts:1862) refuses a recommendation outside the policy's permitted set; and when the policy DOES permit it — I seeded permittedControlActions ['CONTINUE','ACCEPT','PROMOTE_BASELINE'], the validator recommended ACCEPT and PROMOTE_BASELINE, and the AssuranceAssessmentCompleted event recorded both — PromoteBaseline citing that assessment was still REJECTED with NO_EFFECTIVE_PROMOTION_DECISION until a Governance Decision existed. The recommendation is recorded and read by exactly one consumer, the read-model (rph-projections/src/assurance-view.ts:263, field `controlActions`); nothing executes it.

THE SHARPEST LIMB IN THE LANE, AND IT HOLDS — but it takes three sites, none total, so this is MULTI_SITE rather than a single by-construction claim.

I WENT AND LOOKED FOR A FUNCTION, A CLOSURE, OR A CODE PATH SELECTED BY ID, AS INSTRUCTED. There is none. A policy's applicability is an `ApplicabilityRule` (objects.ts:114) whose `expression` is interpreted by a CLOSED EIGHT-ARM DISCRIMINATED UNION — ALL / ANY / NOT / EQUALS / IN / CONTAINS / EXISTS / RISK_AT_LEAST (packages/rph-assurance/src/applicability.ts:12-21) — evaluated by `evaluateApplicability`, a pure recursive interpreter whose `default` arm is a `const _never: never` exhaustiveness guard that THROWS (applicability.ts:82). No id-to-handler table, no registry of predicates, no dynamic import.

SITE 1 — THE DATA DECIDES, AND I DROVE IT. assurance.ts:1319 (`requestAssuranceAssessment`'s applicability block) runs `policyApplicability` with `evaluateApplicability` INJECTED, and refuses when the outcome is NOT_APPLICABLE. Two worlds identical except for ONE DATA VALUE inside the expression: `{op:'EQUALS', path:'$.pwuKind', value:'ARCHITECTURE'}` -> RequestAssuranceAssessment ACCEPTED; `{op:'EQUALS', path:'$.pwuKind', value:'IMPLEMENTATION'}` -> REJECTED naming the yielded §5.2 outcome. A composed expression decides too: `{op:'ALL', operands:[{op:'RISK_AT_LEAST', dimension:'CONSEQUENCE', level:'CRITICAL'}]}` against a HIGH-consequence PWU -> REJECTED. Same site is used by packages/rph-engine/src/governing-policies.ts:67 with the same kernel and the same injected evaluator, so 'which policies govern this PWU' has one answer computed once.

SITE 2 — EXECUTABLE CODE CANNOT REACH THE WIRE, AND I DROVE THAT TOO. packages/rph-contracts/src/hash.ts:74. I dispatched CreateAssurancePolicy with `applicability.expression` set to an actual JavaScript function, in-process, twice — once as the whole expression and once smuggled as an operand of a legal `ALL` — and BOTH were refused before any handler ran, at payload canonicalization: 'Unsupported type for canonicalization: function'. I instrumented the closure: invocation count 0 in both runs. This is the strongest form the limb can take — the forbidden arrangement is not refused by a check that could be deleted, it cannot be serialized.

SITE 3 — DISPOSITION RULES ARE DATA THE ENGINE EVALUATES. `DispositionRuleSchema` is a z.strictObject of scalars and string arrays (objects.ts:210-216), and Gate C (assurance.ts:1908) evaluates it. Driven in three worlds: SATISFIED + OPEN BLOCKING -> REJECTED; REJECTED + the same OPEN BLOCKING -> ACCEPTED; SATISFIED + OPEN ADVISORY -> ACCEPTED. The rule's DATA — the severity, the disposition key — is what changed the outcome.

AND THE ONE ESCAPE HATCH IS INERT. A CODE-SHAPED expression IS storable: `{op:'JS', code:"subject.pwuKind !== 'ARCHITECTURE'"}` was accepted onto the policy and persisted verbatim (the wire schema for the expression is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` — objects.ts:68, a deliberate placeholder). It is never executed: the unknown op hits the exhaustiveness throw, `narrowByExpression`'s try/catch converts it to REQUIRES_HUMAN_DETERMINATION (rph-domain/src/governance.ts:659-670), and `applicabilityPermitsAssessment` admits that outcome — so the smuggled source string had ZERO effect on the decision and the assessment proceeded exactly as if no expression had been written. Fail-permissive, disclosed in situ, and not a violation of THIS limb: the code is not run.

NO SITE IS TOTAL: delete hash.ts:74 and a closure reaches the store; delete assurance.ts:1319 and the applicability data stops deciding; delete Gate C and the disposition rules stop deciding. Three sites, one limb.

THE LIMB HAS TWO CLAIMS AND NEITHER SITE CARRIES BOTH.

(a) 'A VERSIONED ASSURANCE POLICY' — REAL, AND DRIVEN. `floor.reasoning-review` is not a code constant wearing a policy's name: it is an ordinary ASSURANCE_POLICY aggregate created through the ordinary `CreateAssurancePolicy` command (`seedFloorPolicies`, packages/rph-engine/src/seed-workbench.ts:245-263, sends the same payload any user policy takes), and it persists carrying `version: "1.0.0"` and `semanticVersion: 1` alongside `independenceRequirement`, `evaluatorRole` and its nine criteria. I drove the seed and read the object back. It is then LOCKED: `rejectIfFloorLocked` (the cited site) refuses Edit / Supersede / Suspend / Activate on any of the three FLOOR_POLICY_IDS with an RPH_INVARIANT_VIOLATION, and the byte-identical acts on a NON-floor policy carrying the SAME content were all ACCEPTED. So the policy is a governed, versioned, immutable object — the opposite of the 'second prompt' the invariant's title forbids.

(b) 'IMPLEMENTED BY A REPLACEABLE VALIDATOR' — ALSO REAL, at a SECOND site, and also driven. The Validator is a governed object in its own right: `VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_ENTRY` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/validator-registry.ts) carries `supportedPolicies`, which I drove to `["floor.reasoning-review"]`, plus a three-state ACTIVE/DEGRADED/DISABLED machine. `completeAssuranceAssessment` Gate D (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:2145) then REFUSES a WITHDRAWN implementation's result and directs the caller to an ALTERNATE — that refusal IS replaceability with teeth, and the registered ACTIVE alternate was accepted at the same site in the same run. Above it, the in-process seam (`createValidatorRegistry`, packages/rph-assurance/src/validators.ts:99; `createFloorRegistry`, apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/assurance/index.ts:12) swaps agy↔mock keyed ONLY on `policyId`, and `runFloorResults` (validators.ts:300) treats an ABSENT validator as MISSING → the composed aggregate blocks rather than assuming satisfied. The policy therefore outlives, and is never defined by, its validator — canon ASR-1's SCOPE clause ('prompts, models, and deterministic checks are runtime assets of the policy, never the policy itself') made structural.

WHY MULTI_SITE AND NOT DRIVEN: site (a) says nothing whatever about a validator; site (b) never mentions the policy's version and fails OPEN for an UNREGISTERED validatorId (disclosed in its own docblock at assurance.ts:2134: 'AN UNREGISTERED VALIDATOR DOES NOT REFUSE — the disclosed fail-open'). (1) PROFESSIONAL RATIONALE SUMMARIES — WIRED, and properly. `ProfessionalRationaleSummary` is a contracted deliverable the producer RETURNS (packages/rph-assurance/src/validators.ts:43-49: rationale, assumptions, limitations, residualUncertainty), obtained via the agent's `declare_rationale` tool, threaded into `ReasoningReviewInput.rationale` and rendered FIRST in the judge prompt (apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/assurance/reasoning-review-validator.ts:87). (2) OUTPUTS — WIRED. `ReasoningReviewInput.content` is the serialized PWA graph export (apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/floor.ts:318-321).

(3) AUTHORIZED TOOL-CALL RECORDS — NOT REVIEWED, BY DESIGN. The ONLY channel from the producing turn to the reviewer is `narration: planText()` (apps/rph-demo/src/routes/pwa/[id]/agent/+server.ts:131 and :158), and `planText` is `narrationOf(transcript)`, whose entire body is the cited filter: role AGENT **and kind 'message'**. `tool_call` and `tool_result` entries are dropped. `apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/agent/transcript.test.ts:38-42` pins that as intended — its title is 'excludes the user, the system, and tool traffic — the reviewer judges the producer, not the harness' and it asserts `expect(n).not.toContain('define_pwu_type')`. WHAT THE LIMB REQUIRES: above the floor, each material boundary HAS an explicit RISK-DERIVED coverage decision. Two load-bearing words: EXPLICIT (it is recorded, not inferred) and RISK-DERIVED (risk is an input to it).

THE ENFORCED HALF IS REAL AND RISK-CAPABLE. `RequestAssuranceAssessment` runs DOC-004 §5.1/§5.2 applicability at assurance.ts:1302, injecting the DOC-007 §18 expression evaluator (`evaluateApplicability`, assurance.ts:1311), whose op set includes `RISK_AT_LEAST{dimension, level}` resolving `$.riskProfile` (applicability.ts:71). So a policy CAN scope itself by risk, and the seeded HIGH_ASSURANCE profile does exactly that. I drove that gate and it refuses (see the control in `observed`): a policy that does not govern the subject is REJECTED with 'its DOC-004 §5.1 applicability rule yields NOT_APPLICABLE'.

BUT THAT GATE POINTS THE OTHER WAY. It refuses OVER-coverage (assessing under a policy that does not govern). Nothing refuses UNDER-coverage: no site asks whether a material boundary has any above-floor coverage decision at all. Driven: a PWU whose declared riskProfile is the MAXIMUM the contract admits on every dimension — consequence CRITICAL, uncertainty CRITICAL, irreversibility CRITICAL, securitySensitivity HIGH, regulatoryExposure HIGH — and `assurancePolicyIds: []` was accepted, and its plan proposed, approved, activated and STARTED. This kernel answers scope only ... activation is a separate concern and is not silently folded in here.' Deliberate and disclosed — but the consequence is that the ratified risk-condition half of §5.1 has no reader anywhere (census below), leaving RISK_AT_LEAST-inside-`expression` as the only live risk path.

AND 'EXPLICIT' FAILS EVEN WHERE COVERAGE EXISTS. (a) 'PRINCIPLES MAY LEGITIMATELY CONFLICT' — SUPPORTED.   BLOCKING open      -> REJECTED, foreclosed.
  CRITICAL open      -> REJECTED, foreclosed.

'A PROHIBITION MAY BLOCK' — the mechanism exists but not where the limb needs it. `severityIfNotMet` is turned into blocking force at exactly ONE production predicate: `mandatory: BLOCKING_SEVERITIES.has(c.severityIfNotMet)` (validators.ts:229), whose own docblock explains it was hardcoded `true` before and that 'a criterion blocks iff its severity does'. That predicate feeds `dispositionFromFindings` on the DE MINIMIS FLOOR path only; `completeAssuranceAssessment` never reads criterion RESULTS at all (already filed, RPH-ASR-004 and RPH-ASR-005). So a criterion authored BLOCKING blocks nothing at the command surface.

'A HEURISTIC RAISES A QUESTION' — no shape. There is no question, query, inquiry or open-item object. Driven: a RECOMMENDATION at ADVISORY was recorded OPEN and the assessment then completed SATISFIED with `observationIds: []` and `residualUncertainty: []` on the completion event. Nothing was raised, asked or carried forward.

'A SMELL TRIGGERS INVESTIGATION WITHOUT PRESUMING A DEFECT' — REFUSED BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THIS IS THE DRIVEN CORE OF THE ROW. The engine's only 'investigate' consequence is `escalationRules.escalateOnOpenSeverities`, and the cited site restricts it to `ESCALATABLE_SEVERITIES = new Set(['CRITICAL'])` (assurance.ts:97). Authoring a policy that says 'investigate when an ADVISORY signal is open' is REJECTED. So is INFORMATIONAL. So is MATERIAL. So is BLOCKING. Only CRITICAL is accepted — and CRITICAL is itself a member of `BLOCKING_SEVERITIES`, so the one severity that can trigger investigation is also the one that forecloses satisfaction. Investigation and presumption-of-defect are welded to the same value: a smell cannot have the first without the second.

AND THE ESCAPE HATCH THE REFUSAL NAMES IS A DEAD POINTER. The message directs the author to 'express it through the ratified EscalationRule.trigger (§13), not this field'. `EscalationRule.trigger` is `z.unknown()` (objects.ts:219) and is never evaluated: census below returns zero evaluators against a live control on `escalationTarget`. So the documented alternative route to a soft-tier investigation does not exist either.

AND THERE IS NO EPISTEMIC-STATUS FIELD AT ALL. `AssessmentCriterion` (objects.ts:126-135) is id, name, description, criterionType, evaluationMethod, requiredEvidenceIds, severityIfNotMet, mayBeNotApplicable. `criterionType` is BOOLEAN/ENUMERATED/QUALITATIVE/QUANTITATIVE/COMPOSITE (enums.ts:333) — a SHAPE axis, not an epistemic one. So a prohibition, a heuristic and a smell are authored identically and are distinguishable only by a five-value severity that collapses to a Boolean at the one predicate that reads it.

evidence:
I FORMALIZED A CORRELATION AS A POLICY FINDING, THEN UPGRADED IT TO A BLOCKER ON THE WIRE, AND THE ENGINE TOOK IT.

THE SETUP IS CANON'S OWN EXAMPLE. The policy declared a `FindingDefinition` with code LONG_METHOD_SMELL, description 'An empirical smell: long methods correlate with defects. Investigate; do not presume a defect.', and `defaultSeverity: 'INFORMATIONAL'` — i.e. the policy states, in ratified DOC-004 §9.1 form, that this finding carries signal weight and no more. That is the 'compiled smell' and the 'correlation' of canon's sentence, written down.

THE UPGRADE. `RecordAssuranceObservation{observationType:'FINDING', findingCode:'LONG_METHOD_SMELL', severity:'CRITICAL'}` was ACCEPTED and persisted verbatim (severity=CRITICAL, findingCode=LONG_METHOD_SMELL). The policy's own declaration of the finding's weight is not consulted, not compared, not even loaded. The completion at SATISFIED was then foreclosed on that CRITICAL — so the upgraded weight did not merely sit in the store, it CHANGED AN AUTHORITATIVE OUTCOME. A correlation became a hard block in one dispatch.

THE HANDLER MAKES EXACTLY ONE CHECK, WHICH IS THE ANCHOR. `recordAssuranceObservation` (assurance.ts:2339) loads the assessment, refuses if it does not exist (the cited line), and then builds the observation state directly from the payload — `findingCode: p.findingCode ?? p.observationType, observationType: p.observationType, severity: p.severity`. It never loads the ASSURANCE_POLICY, so `findingDefinitions[].defaultSeverity` has no reader on this path. Confirmed by a second control: an entirely UNDECLARED finding code, `NO_SUCH_CODE_ANYWHERE`, was also accepted — the policy does not constrain the code, let alone its weight.

A SECOND INSTANCE, ABOVE THE SEAM, AND THIS ONE IS FILED IN ITS OWN DOCBLOCK. The PWA policy-authoring textarea mints every NEW criterion at `severityIfNotMet: 'BLOCKING'` (policy-fields.ts:47). Its docblock records the history in canon's own terms: 'severityIfNotMet: every criterion reset to BLOCKING, PROMOTING the ADVISORY criteria of all six additive policies to blocking. That changes what those policies MEAN — assurance-rules maps a BLOCKING criterion's NOT_MET to REJECTED, while an ADVISORY one does not affect the disposition. Nothing about editing a policy's wording should make it stricter.' Reuse-by-description now preserves prior criteria, but the residual is disclosed verbatim: 'The other four levels stay unreachable from this textarea — the residual cost of the Boolean this replaces, and the reason a per-criterion severity control is the natural follow-up.' So the one authoring surface a professional actually uses can only produce blocking criteria: formalizing a heuristic through the workbench necessarily upgrades it.

WHY UNENFORCED_OBSERVED_ADMISSION RATHER THAN PARTIAL_DIVERGENT_FILED. The surface instance is filed; the ENGINE instance is not. I drove the engine and it accepted the upgrade, so the arm follows the drive.

WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: evidence SUPPORTING a claim outside its declared scope, absent an explicit assessment. Two things therefore had to be arranged, and both were: support outside scope, and no explicit assessment.

THE DRIVE. (1) AssertClaim, FITNESS: 'The entire payment system is fit for production use.' -> ACCEPTED. (2) ProposeEvidence, a TEST_RESULT whose declared `scope` is 'unit test of the login button label, happy path only', naming that claim in `supportsClaimIds` -> ACCEPTED. (3) AdmitEvidence with `admittedScope: 'the entire payment system, all environments'` — the caller silently widening the scope by an order of magnitude at the moment of admission — and that claim in `admittedClaimIds` -> ACCEPTED, status ADMISSIBLE, and the stored `scope` is STILL the unit-test string, so the two are simply never compared. (4) RecordClaimAssessment -> UNDER_ASSESSMENT -> ACCEPTED. (5) RecordClaimAssessment -> SUPPORTED -> ACCEPTED. The FITNESS claim about an entire payment system is now SUPPORTED, and the engine's own derived support set for it is `["evd_...R06"]` — the login-button unit test. That fifth step is what takes this past the arrangement already on file, which stops at the admission: canon's verb is SUPPORT, and I drove the support.

THE SECOND HALF — 'WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT ASSESSMENT' — IS AN UNCHECKED STRING. `AdmitEvidence.admissibilityAssessmentId` is `z.string()` (messages.ts:198) and is echoed onto the event (assurance.ts:547) and never resolved. DRIVEN: an id naming NOTHING -> ACCEPTED, status ADMISSIBLE, and `store.loadObject('asm_...ZZZ')` is undefined; and the EMPTY STRING — no assessment cited at all -> ACCEPTED, status ADMISSIBLE, event payload `"admissibilityAssessmentId":""`. So the exception clause canon attaches to the prohibition cannot be distinguished from its own absence.

WHY THERE IS NO PREDICATE TO CALL DEAD: unlike limbs 4 and 5, no line anywhere compares a scope to a claim's breadth — the register says so in its own words ('No kernel predicate compares evidence scope to claim breadth') and my reader census confirms `admittedScope` has no consumer. WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: letting an execution trace stand as support for the proposition that the OUTCOME SATISFIES INTENT, when all it shows is that execution occurred. WHAT THE CODE DOES: nothing anywhere relates an Evidence object's evidenceType to the proposition it is offered for. I drove the conflation on TWO planes and it was accepted on both.

PLANE 1 — CLAIM SUPPORT. ProposeEvidence(evidenceType:'TRACE', scope:'execution trace of step S1: the step ran to completion') -> ACCEPTED; AdmitEvidence(admittedScope: the same string) -> ACCEPTED, evidence.status=ADMISSIBLE; then RecordClaimAssessment(SUPPORTED) against a FITNESS claim whose statement is literally 'The delivered outcome satisfies the approved Product Intent.' -> ACCEPTED, claim.status=SUPPORTED with supportingEvidenceIds naming the trace. The engine now records, authoritatively, that an intent-satisfaction claim is SUPPORTED and that its support is an execution trace.

PLANE 2 — EVIDENCE REQUIREMENTS. A policy declaring requiredEvidence [{id:'EV-1', evidenceType:'TEST_RESULT', cardinality:'AT_LEAST_ONE', requiredForDispositions:'SATISFIED_ONLY'}]; I proposed and admitted an Evidence object whose actual evidenceType is TRACE and submitted it as satisfying EV-1 with the payload's free-string evidenceType:'TEST_RESULT'. ACCEPTED. store.loadObject(E2).state.evidenceType still reads TRACE. CompleteAssuranceAssessment(SATISFIED) then ACCEPTED and the assessment reached SATISFIED — the TEST_RESULT requirement discharged by a trace. SubmitEvidenceForAssessmentPayloadSchema types evidenceType as z.string().optional() and the handler (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:1480-1600) never loads the Evidence object to compare it.

WHY THE ARM. The refusal machinery on both commands is alive and discriminating (see sibling_control), so this is admission, not absence of a site. `evidenceType` is written and copied and never once compared (census).

NOT DOUBLE-COUNTED WITH ASR-6:6. ASR-6's last sentence ('Evidence cannot support a claim outside its declared scope without an explicit assessment') owns the general scope-vs-claim comparison and RPH-EVD-004 files that gap for passing tests. THIS limb is a TYPE/PROPOSITION conflation, not a scope-breadth one: the trace's scope was stated fully and accurately ('the step ran to completion') and it still supported 'the outcome satisfies intent'. Nothing in the register or the ledger names a trace, an execution artifact, or the execution-occurred/intent-satisfied distinction on the EVIDENCE plane.
